task.title: Authenticate over HTTPS
task.shortdesc: Sign in to an HTTPS remote with a personal access token, or a username and password.

context.p: The first time an operation needs credentials for an HTTPS remote, the Git Client opens a login dialog box. It stores what you enter and reuses it for that server.

ul.li: Personal access token - Recommended, and required by GitHub and for any account with two-factor authentication enabled.
Basic authentication - A username and password, where the server still allows it.

info.note: GitHub no longer accepts account passwords for Git operations. Generate a personal access token and use it instead. For Bitbucket, create an API token with the required scopes and use it as the password with your Bitbucket username. See if a sign-in is rejected.

result.p: The Git Client stores the credentials for that server and stops prompting. To review or remove them later, see .
